feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms, tools, and project examples (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, AI search, studio buildout).  
- Writing is polished and generally error-free, with a strong strategic tone suited to senior digital transformation roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to create a tighter structure and improve scanability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: business impact, efficiency gains, engagement growth, campaign results, cost savings, adoption rates, or team size managed.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and list punctuation (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” uses a serial comma while some other lists do not). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive value will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Simplify the list slightly; “platforms, governance models and content operations” is strong, but the second sentence becomes crowded.
- Use “website” instead of “web” if you want closer alignment with the experience section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are repeated elsewhere, so avoid expanding them further in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and grouped around senior-level strengths rather than restating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; e.g. use all noun phrases and avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” inconsistently.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and workflow/platform integration.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space is tight, replace “public-sector” with “mission-driven” only if targeting broader roles beyond government/associations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with header and Recent Projects.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and “Multi-channel communications operations” repeat Topline Skills and multiple role bullets.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently with action + platform + outcome.
- Tighten wording: e.g., “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Replace generic phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with more concrete value, such as scalability, reuse, or audience engagement.
- Standardize style and punctuation across items; “10×20-foot” is fine, but keep all entries parallel in tense and structure.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current NACo roles in Work Experience.
- Consider keeping only 2–3 projects here or emphasizing unique project details not stated elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, transformation work, and outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“build and refine,” “deliver,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics,” “launched modular campaign experiences,” “improved governance and usability.”
- Consolidate technical detail into 3–4 bullets; e.g. one bullet for Drupal/campaign builds, one for governance/operations, one for AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search success, engagement or traffic improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” substantially repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize post-employment consulting scope and specific initiatives instead.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this item higher-level and let Projects hold the build details.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize executive ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Prioritize the biggest wins first and make outcomes explicit: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on systems work: “Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving executive reporting and data-informed planning.”
- Combine lower-value bullets: merge governance/publishing standards with cross-department planning; add any budget/team-size/vendor metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio bullet may overlap with older video-production entries; frame it as building organizational capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify what was scaled or improved.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy distribution for county-official audiences.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable workflow/editorial impact if available: e.g., publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, cross-team participation, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this entry focused on execution rather than enterprise leadership.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role; clarify what expanded or changed at this level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the most senior, differentiating strengths and use tighter phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior-level language tied to recent work:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization  
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)  
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & stakeholder communications  
- Audience strategy, content planning & user-centered storytelling
- Consider dropping “audience-focused” for “user-centered” or “audience strategy” to sound more concrete.
- Keep each line parallel in structure; avoid mixing broad functions with vague descriptors.
- If space allows elsewhere, move measurable proof to experience bullets rather than this skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat almost verbatim from Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already well established in the header and NACo experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat every platform and language.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, not inventory-led: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current work.
- Consider replacing generic “SharePoint” and “Power Pages” with “Microsoft web platforms” if those are not major recent differentiators.
- If possible, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “enterprise CMS modernization for 10,000+ page public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all tools here repeat the Technical + IT section; keep this version broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary, so avoid overusing the exact phrase.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and doesn’t yet signal seniority or business impact. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic use of analytics rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the strategic items first: lead with “Analytics strategy,” “KPI framework design,” and “Executive reporting,” then list tools.
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support” for stronger senior-level language.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “cross-channel performance measurement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; Topline Skills should be more strategic, Technical + IT more tool-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities and using more specific phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with: **Broadcast & Event Production** — Video production and post-production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Hybrid, virtual and in-person event delivery
- Consider elevating the most senior/recent angle: swap “Video production and editing” for **Broadcast-quality studio production** or **In-house studio buildout and operations**
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid mixing broad and narrow terms; “Livestreaming” → **Livestream and webcast production** is stronger and more professional
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to impact: **Scalable event production workflows** or **Advocacy video programming**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet about building an in-house studio, so keep this skills line concise rather than descriptive

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and repeats the same platform names already shown under “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this space to signal depth or recency—especially Drupal—rather than restating tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent platform first and add level cues: **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially relevant to recent roles; replace with a more impactful platform qualifier or leave a tighter 4-item list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry **Web Platforms & Technical Execution** almost exactly.
- “Power Pages” also overlaps with broader Microsoft tooling already implied elsewhere; keep only if used meaningfully in recent work.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools tied to recent work and grouping older/basic skills more tightly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Lightweight engineering & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more senior.
- Order by relevance to recent work: APIs, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, then HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery.
- If space allows, add scope/context instead of more tools, e.g., “for Drupal-based public-sector sites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may partially overlap with analytics/tooling; ensure it’s not repeated in a separate analytics item.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and group by function to feel more intentional: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, rename to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match your leadership profile.
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and system-building impact; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana, and de-emphasize older/general collaboration tools if needed.
- If you want stronger value, add one short qualifier elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate,” since outcomes can’t be shown in this list alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless central to operations leadership; cut first if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms, but this item is too bare and reads like a vendor list. It should better signal enterprise email/engagement capability while staying consistent with the stronger email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to increase value: **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Optional rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email automation, newsletter publishing, segmentation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Your work experience already establishes email leadership (“newsletters reaching tens of thousands”); avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add a distinct technical angle such as automation, segmentation, or member engagement systems.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; keep this item focused specifically on email/member platform tools.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and recent NACo experience. Use it to sharpen technical specificity, not restate broad capabilities.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace vague terms like **A/B testing** and **Dashboarding** with stronger, more technical phrasing such as **Experimentation** / **Conversion testing** and **BI reporting** / **Executive dashboards**
- Consider ordering by depth/relevance to recent work: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity, Google Tag Manager, SEO analysis, Experimentation**
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes to experience bullets instead of this skills line, e.g. analytics stack supporting reporting for a **10,000+ page site** and **3.5M annual page views**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**
- “Dashboarding” also repeats the reporting/infrastructure language already used in recent NACo roles

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/reach of weekly video updates, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening”; replace with specific actions such as “produced,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “trained,” or “supervised.”
- Consider: “Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video series, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching or early producing of the series.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; keep this version focused on foundational team-building and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, stakeholders/program teams served, or audience/reach.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the CV naturally weights more recent leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia entries; avoid repeating broad production language.
- Since later roles already show digital leadership growth, don’t overstate this one as a full digital management role.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed skills/tasks list than a polished tools entry. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already emphasized elsewhere, so this section should stay concise and software-focused.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize tools first, then tightly grouped production capabilities.
